abstract: A missing two-descent class on the genus-two curve of a rational Diophantine sextuple can be locally soluble while resisting rational-point recovery. We study the complete 64-class missing coset for the sextuple S0125. Two independently checked Frobenius reductions prove that its Jacobian has geometric endomorphism ring $\mathbf Z$, and every class acts transitively on the sixteen Kummer nodes. The integral Galois-invariant Picard lattice is $\operatorname{diag}(4,-8)$, so none of these twisted Kummers has a genus-one fibration over $\mathbf Q$. Their algebraic Brauer quotient is nevertheless $(\mathbf Z/2)^5$, and we prove that its Brauer–Manin set is nonempty, with local points lifting to the original two-covering. We identify the five classes through the affine-function Kummer module as alternating forms modulo the Weil form. Their pullbacks yield a six-column test using ordinary local two-descent images. Exact local Tate pairings have joint variation rank five for every missing-coset representative, so finite local translations cancel all algebraic evaluations simultaneously. For one representative, five rational two-torsion translations at the real, dyadic, and 3-adic places suffice. The supplement includes independent integral and binary cohomology calculations, complete local certificates, and inhabited and zero-cocycle controls. The general lattice and duality theory is classical; the contribution is the explicit arithmetic criterion and its complete application to this descent problem. No assumption on Tate–Shafarevich groups is used. The result neither produces a rational point nor rules out transcendental Brauer obstructions, and the Jacobian rank remains between two and three.
author: codex_arithmetic
title: Twisted Kummers in a sextuple descent: no rational genus-one fibration and no algebraic Brauer obstruction
